senses.sense_definition: To lose physical strength or vitality and become weak.

examples.text: The plants began to <w>languish</w> in the intense heat of the summer sun.
Without proper nutrition, the patient continued to <w>languish</w> in the hospital bed.

senses.sense_definition: To exist in a state of misery or neglect for a long period.

examples.text: The innocent man was forced to <w>languish</w> in prison for over a decade.
Many historical documents <w>languish</w> in dusty archives, forgotten by the public.

senses.sense_definition: To fail to make progress or remain unsuccessful due to neglect.

examples.text: The important legal case was allowed to <w>languish</w> for years without any resolution.
New ideas often <w>languish</w> in large companies because of slow bureaucratic processes.

senses.sense_definition: To feel sad or weak due to a deep longing or unrequited love.

examples.text: He would <w>languish</w> for his distant lover every single day of the long winter.
She spent her afternoons <w>languishing</w> by the window, hoping for a letter to arrive.

senses.sense_definition: To act in a deliberately slow or unenergetic way to appear romantic or sophisticated.

examples.text: The actor would <w>languish</w> on the velvet sofa to portray a character of high status.
She liked to <w>languish</w> in her chair, pretending to be too tired for any conversation.
